 Elle Fanning as Effie Trinket in 'The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping' 
 Murray Close/Lionsgate 
 EXCLUSIVE: A fire continues to burn for Lionsgate ‘s The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping when it comes to its presales, which we now understand are well ahead of Universal’s Wicked . 
 In addition, advance tickets are the best that Lionsgate has ever seen post-Covid for any title. Yes, Sunrise on the Reaping is ahead of Michael which bowed to $97.2M in North America.

 ‘Hunger Games: Sunrise On The Reaping’ Cast Vs. Past Actors From Previous Films 
 Prediction platform Polymarket believes there’s a 75% chance that the feature take of Suzanne Collins’ 2025 novel will open to north of $100M . There are other distribution sources who also agree. But given that female driven movies can often be front-loaded, the floor for the Francis Lawrence directed prequel is now at $80M+ (up from last weekend’s forecast of $60M-$70M). Note, there was also a concern two years ago that Wicked would be front-loaded, however those presales translated into a $112.5M opening. Depending on the demographic and genre of the movie, there’s not necessarily a direct line between presales and an enormous box office opening. 
 That said, 2024 predecessor The Hunger Games: The Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes is no longer a comp here to Sunrise on the Reaping as far as presales go . Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes was hindered by the actors strike and based on a Collins novel which wasn’t as popular as its predecessors. The prequel, which was the origin story about the series most notorious character, Coriolanus Snow, opened to $44.6M stateside, the lowest in the franchise. The movie wound up doing a 3.7x multiple for a final $166.3M domestic. Songbirds and Snakes received a B+ CinemaScore next to the franchise’s previous As and A-s. 
 Watch on Deadline 
 With nothing of the blockbuster magnitude of Wicked, Moana 2 or Zootopia 2 on the horizon at the Thanksgiving box office, Sunrise on the Reaping is shaping up to deliver the goods. It would not be a surprise if the Jesse Plemons, Elle Fanning, Mckenna Grace, Joseph Zada, Ralph Fiennes ensemble also wins the 5-day Thanksgiving box office against newcomers, Disney Animation’s Hexed and Universal/Paramount’s Ariana Grande starring Focker-in-Law, which are both looking at $40M-$50M apiece.
